The Ti 2ZrMo0.5Nb0.5 high-entropy alloy studied in this paper was prepared by vacuum induction melting technology with high-purity materials (≥99 wt.%), including Ti bar, zirconium sponge, molybdenum flakes and niobium flakes, in a water-cooled copper crucible under argon atmosphere. The ingot was smelted under electromagnetic stirring to ensure the chemical uniformity and finally got a cylindrical specimen with a size of Ф50 × 40 mm.

The room temperature compression experiment of Ti 2ZrMo0.5Nb0.5 high-entropy alloy was carried out on the electronic universal material test machine Instron5500R 200 kN, the compression rate was set to 0.6 mm/min. The sample was the cylindrical sample of Ф8 × 12 mm.

The hot compression tests were carried out on the Gleeble 1500 thermal simulation testing machine with the cylindrical samples of Ф8 × 12 mm. During the thermal simulation experiment, the deformation was set to 50%, the heating rate was 10 °C s−1, and the sample was heated to the experimental temperature and kept for 5 min to ensure that the temperature of each part of the sample remained uniform during the experiment. To reduce the influence of the friction heat generated by the two end faces of the samples, graphite sheets were placed on the two end faces during the experiment. In this paper, different deformation temperatures (from 900°C to 1150°C, the fixed strain rate of 0.01 s−1) and different strain rates (from 0.001 s−1 to 0.1 s−1, the fixed temperature of 1150°C) were set to reveal the effect of temperatures and strain rates on the hot deformation microstructure and properties.
